title: Droll Stories
author: Honoré de Balzac
current_text: Canada Customs banned Droll Stories beginning in 1914, and the book was subject to confiscation as late as 1970. Droll Stories was banned for obscenity from 1901 to 1923 and again from 1928 to approximately 1973. In New Zealand, a Magistrate's Court banned Droll Stories in 1935. In 1935, a bookseller was convicted under the 1910 Act for displaying Droll Stories; the magistrate said the work was indecent because its tales glorified immorality and licentiousness and ridiculed purity and virtue.

ban_rows.note: Per Wikipedia's NZ list, Droll Stories was on the Customs prohibited list and a magistrate's court banned it in 1935; it is now unrestricted.

Balzac's bawdy 1832–37 collection of medieval-style tales — long a target of obscenity prosecutions across the Anglosphere — was added to the Irish Register of Prohibited Publications in 1953 under the 1929 Censorship of Publications Act for "obscene material of a sexual nature."
